================================================================================
NORMATIVE EXERCISE CONTENT FORMAT  ("exercise markdown", extension .ex.md)
This section is the single source of truth. It is reproduced verbatim in every M2 task
prompt that touches the format. Implement it exactly; do not extend it silently.
================================================================================

FILE SHAPE
  One file = one DECK (a small ordered group of exercises from one part of one chapter).
  Path: content/exercises/NN-slug.ex.md   (flat directory; NN is two digits, reading order only)
  Order of decks is content/exercises/INDEX -- one filename per line, '#' comments, blank
  lines ignored.

  # Choosing a bank

  deck: pad-play-banks
  chapter: Part: Pad play
  summary: Select BANK 1 in Performance mode and read the bank indicator.
  cite: guide-book 15 "First, select BANK 1"

  Before you start, turn the unit on and let the `SXC-1` logo disappear.

  ## Which button returns you to BANK 1

  type: quiz
  id: pad-play-bank-a-button
  cite: guide-book 15 "press the `A` button"
  tags: banks, performance-mode

  The display shows `D:4` and the `D` button is lit. Which single button do you press
  to start selecting BANK 1?

  - [x] `A`
  - [ ] `B`
  - [ ] `EDIT`
  - [ ] The up directional button

  ### Why

  Pressing `A` shows `SELECT BANK 1` on the display.

GRAMMAR (line-oriented, applied to the whole file)
  deck title          first non-blank line, ^# +(.*\S)\s*$        exactly ONE '#' in the file
  exercise            ^## +(.*\S)\s*$                             text is the learner-facing title
  role                ^### +(.*\S)\s*$                            starts a role block
  field               ^([a-z][a-z0-9-]*): ?(.*)$                   only inside a field block
  field continuation  a line indented >= 2 spaces inside a field block; appended to the
                      previous field's value separated by one space
  field block         the maximal run of field lines immediately following a #/##/### heading
                      (blank lines allowed BEFORE it, never INSIDE it)
  body                everything after the field block up to the next ## or ###; parsed as
                      Markdown BLOCKS by M1's parser (briefs/M1-plan.md section 4.5), unchanged
  choices             a top-level GFM task list ^- \[([ xX])\] +(.*\S)\s*$ inside an exercise
                      body; its items are removed from the body and become the option list

  HOW PROSE IS PARSED -- bind to the real committed API, not to a description of it:
    body blocks       parseBlocksEngine 0 False [] bodyLines
    single-line fields parseInline 0 value            (summary, check, option labels, titles)
  pageCount is 0 ON PURPOSE (probe P-H): it makes parseInline NEVER emit a PageRef, so a bare
  `p. N` in exercise prose stays literal text and EVERY manual link goes through an explicit
  cite:/find: with a slug. A bare page number is ambiguous across four documents, and this is
  also what makes E-LOOKUP-SPOILER meaningful. consumesSlugs is False with an empty supply, so
  exercise prose never needs and never perturbs an anchor-slug supply.

  Prose therefore supports **bold**, *em*, `code`, *[Figure: ...]* placeholders, tables,
  blockquotes and nested lists exactly as the manuals do.

  STRUCTURAL HEADINGS are detected with headingLineOf on the RAW, UNSTRIPPED line, which is
  column-0 only (probe P-I: headingLineOf "   ### X" = Nothing). Levels 1-3 at column 0 are
  structural (deck / exercise / role); levels 4-6 stay in the body and block-parse as ordinary
  Heading blocks. An INDENTED `#{1,6} ` line anywhere in exercise prose is the error
  E-BODY-INDENTED-HEADING: whether it becomes a Heading depends on subtle indent and
  blank-line shape (probe P-K measured an indent-3 `###` under `1. ` folding into a paragraph,
  which renders as literal hash marks), and exercise content must not depend on that.

  CHOICE LISTS ARE LIFTED FROM THE RAW BODY LINES BEFORE BLOCK PARSING. There is no task-list
  construct in the content model: `- [x] \`A\`` parses as an ordinary Bullets item whose inline
  content still literally begins "[x] " (probe P-J). So scan the raw body lines with
  bulletItemOf, take the maximal run whose content starts "[x] " or "[ ] ", remove those lines
  from the body, and parse each option label with parseInline 0. bulletItemOf is NOT currently
  exported from SXC1.Content.Markdown -- widen that export list.

  An `Unparsed` block anywhere in exercise prose is the error E-BLOCK-UNPARSED. Note that with
  the real classifyLine this is UNREACHABLE from any file (ParaShape is a genuine catch-all),
  so it is a `seam`-class code: see the coverage classes below.

DECK FIELDS
  deck     REQUIRED  [a-z0-9-]+, globally unique, STABLE FOREVER (M3 keys progress by it)
  chapter  REQUIRED  a chapter title from the course map of content/exercise-inventory.md,
                     which the validator PARSES from that file's `### Chapter N - <title>`
                     headings (strip the trailing parenthetical). That yields
                       0 Front matter / 1 Part: Preparation / 2 Part: Pad play /
                       3 Part: Sampling / 4 Part: Sequencer / 5 Part: Leveling up
                     and the validator additionally asserts chapters 1-5 equal the guide-book
                     part titles from Outline.outPartTitles and appear in the glossary. Three
                     independent sources must agree, and NOTHING is hard-coded in Haskell.
                     `Front matter` is admissible (it is chapter 0 of the inventory and a UI
                     label M1's outline already uses), so front-matter content in a later
                     milestone needs no format change.
